name: The Ext3 File System
description:
ext3, or third extended filesystem, is a journaled file system that is commonly used by the Linux kernel. ext3 adds the following features to ext2:
  • A journal - which is used to maintain consistency after unclean shutdown.
  • Online file system growth.
  • HTree indexing for larger directories.
Do you know who created ext3 file system?
answer: Dr. Stephen C. Tweedie is a software developer who is known for his work on the Linux kernel, in particular his work on filesystems.

name: Creating an Ext3 File System
description:
The steps for creating an ext3 file system are as follows:

1. Format the partition with the ext3 file system using mkfs.ext3.


mkfs.ext3 /dev/ubdb 
 Filesystem label= OS type: Linux Block size=4096 (log=2) Fragment size=4096 (log=2) Stride=0 blocks, Stripe width=0 blocks 393216 inodes, 1572864 blocks 78643 blocks (5.00%) reserved for the super user First data block=0 Maximum filesystem blocks=1610612736 48 block groups 32768 blocks per group, 32768 fragments per group 8192 inodes per group Superblock backups stored on blocks: 32768, 98304, 163840, 229376, 294912, 819200, 884736 Writing inode tables: done Creating journal (32768 blocks): done Writing superblocks and filesystem accounting information: done This filesystem will be automatically checked every 27 mounts or 180 days, whichever comes first. Use tune2fs -c or -i to override.
2. Optionally, Label the file system using e2label.
e2label /dev/ubdb ext3fs
Verify with
blkid 
 /dev/ubdb: LABEL="ext3fs" UUID="490c22e4-8844-462c-93af-5dd2482e6b20" SEC_TYPE=" ext2" TYPE="ext3"
We will mount the newly created ext3fs like:
mkdir /ext3data

mount /dev/ubdb /ext3data

name: Ext2 File System
description:
Lets say we have ext2 file system:
mkfs.ext2 /dev/ubdc

mkdir /old_ext2data

mount /dev/ubdc /old_ext2data
Last two lines on
mount
output shows appropriate file systems. 
 /dev/ubdb on /ext3data type ext3 (rw) /dev/ubdc on /old_ext2data type ext2 (rw)
we created 100 directories with single file on each directory on ext2.
for i in {1..100}; do mkdir /old_ext2data/dir$i; date > /old_ext2data/dir$i/f$i.txt; done

name: Converting Ext2 to an Ext3 File System
description:
We have ext2 filesystem mounted on old_ext2data after few months, we realized its better have a journal support. We want to convert this to ext3fs. Thankfully, tune2fs allows you to convert an ext2 file system to ext3. Always use the e2fsck utility to check your file system before and after using tune2fs To convert an ext2 file system to ext3,type the following command:
e2fsck /dev/ubdc

tune2fs -j block_device

e2fsck/dev/ubdc
where block_device contains the ext2 file system you wish to convert. now unmount and remount the file system
umount /old_ext2data

mount /dev/ubdc /old_ext2data
and run
mount
can you spot the change? 
/dev/ubdb on /ext3data type ext3 (rw)                                           
/dev/ubdc on /old_ext2data type ext3 (rw)

name: Revert a partition from Ext3 to Ext2
description:
If you wish to revert a partition from ext3 to ext2 for any reason, you must first unmount the ext3 partition by typing,
umount /old_ext2data

Next, change the file system type to ext2 by typing the following command as root:
tune2fs -O ^has_journal /d ev/ubdc

Check the partition for errors by typing the following com mand as root:
e2fsck -y /dev/ubdc

Then mount the partition again as ext2 file system by typing:
mount -t ext2 /dev/ubdc /old_ext2data

Note

If a .journal file exists at the root level of the partition, delete it.
You now have an ext2 partition.
